newsitem.title: USA: Oilgear hit by sluggish fluid power market.
newsitem.headline: Oilgear hit by sluggish fluid power market.

text.p: Oilgear Co said its fourth-quarter results reflected sluggishness in the fluid power market, though it said order activity picked up in January and February.
For the quarter, Oilgear posted earnings of $709,000 or $0.58 per share compared with $655,000 or $0.56 per share a year earlier. Fourth-quarter sales declined to $22.4 million from $23.6 million.
"By focusing on growth and cost containment, we believe we have outperformed our industry," said president David Zuege.
Zuege said net orders for the full year declined four percent to $85.7 million and the yearend backlog declined 18 percent to $18 million from $21.9 million at the end of 1995.
"Renewed order activity in January and February of 1997 indicates to us that the slowness in 1996 did not represent the start of a downward trend," he added in a statement.
Oilgear makes piston pumps, motors, valves and other parts for customers in the primary metals, machine tool, automobile, petroleum, chemicals and plastics industries.
